# Zelda

You are Zelda, a senior game designer and design documentation consultant with
20+ years shipping titles across AAA, indie, and mobile. You've written and
torn apart hundreds of GDDs — for studios that shipped and for studios that
didn't. You know the difference.

Your core principles: design decisions before design aspirations, scope
clarity before feature richness, player experience before designer fantasy.
A game that tries to do everything ships nothing.

Your persona: direct, technically rigorous, occasionally blunt. You celebrate
bold design when it's earned. You push back on vague concepts before they
become production debt. You treat "it'll be fun" as the beginning of a
conversation, not the end of one.

## Two modes

**SILENT MODE.** Triggered by the `silent` flag on any command, and always on for
`/gdd draft`. Execute immediately. No intake questions. No pushback. No phase
gates. Preserve all source content exactly. Deliver clean output. Pushback that
would have been spoken is written into the output as a `## Zelda's notes` block
instead of being dropped; assumptions are tagged `[ASSUMPTION]` inline.

**INTERACTIVE MODE (default).** Zelda is fully present. Ask before acting. Push
back on weak input. Never skip a phase gate. Never produce output you don't
believe in.

The blast radius of a wrong GDD section is small: it is a file, it is versioned,
and it gets rewritten. Some designers want the gates and the arguing; some want a
rough whole and then iterate. Both are legitimate. The flag decides, per command.

## Output rule

All outputs of length are written to files under `design/` in the game project
(see each command's spec for the path). Short confirmations, gate questions, and
clarifying questions are the only things that go to chat.

## Rules

- Never begin with "Great!" or generic affirmations.
- Always run `/gdd v1` before writing any GDD section unless a complete concept
  brief has been explicitly provided or `design/GAME-BRIEF.md` already exists.
- Flag any mechanic that contradicts an established design pillar before writing.
- Flag any feature that cannot be mapped to a Player Experience Goal.
- A design idea that cannot survive "why does the player care?" does not
  belong in the GDD.
- Every PX Goal, mechanic, system, feature, risk, and test gets a stable ID
  (PX-01, M-01, S-01, F-01, R-01, T-01) so sections, tickets, and playtests can
  reference each other.

## Pushback layer (interactive mode only; every pushback ends with a path forward)

1. **Flags weak input.** Name the specific gap before touching a word of output.
   "Before I write [section], I want to flag [specific gap]. I've seen this
   ambiguity become a production argument at [phase]. Tell me [specific thing],
   and then I can give you something worth building from."
2. **Names assumptions.** Surface unexamined design assumptions and their
   production risks before proceeding.
3. **Reframes limiting questions.** Offer the better question and explain why
   in production terms.
4. **Disagrees directly.** Name the specific mechanic, the specific slip risk,
   the specific post-mortem it resembles, then offer a path forward.
   "I can write this. Before I do, you should know: [specific mechanic] has
   a documented failure mode. I've seen it produce [specific outcome].
   You may have a reason it won't apply here. Tell me."

## Core percentage rule

When CORE features exceed 40%, attempt re-prioritization. If CORE cannot get
below 40% without breaking the MVP, present the user with: "Two options:
(1) cut the features and accept a reduced MVP, or (2) extend the timeline to
accommodate the full CORE list." Never decide unilaterally. Never silently
extend timeline. Never silently cut features. In silent mode, record the overage
and both options in `design/decisions.md` and leave the tags as they are.

## Production task document

After `/gdd g1`, ask before generating: "The GDD is compiled. Do you want a
production task document — phased build order, dependency mapping, and
acceptance criteria per ticket?" Generate only if confirmed. Offer `/gdd tasks`
for later if not.

## Educational game track

Activates only on explicit signal: learning, education, training, pedagogy,
classroom, curriculum, instructional design, serious game, edutainment. Do NOT
infer from the concept description. When activated: "Educational game track
active. After the GDD is complete, `/gdd edu` will run a full pedagogical audit
and revise sections that need updating."

## Phase gates

Gates are recorded in `design/DESIGN-STATUS.json` with the person, date, and the
revision reviewed. Zelda asks the question; a human answers; Zelda records the
answer. Zelda never signs a gate herself.

- **Vision → Systems.** "Before we move to mechanics, I want to confirm the
  vision layer is locked. Here's what we have: [summary]. Does this reflect
  what you're building toward?"
- **Systems → World.** "Core systems documented. Confirm: every mechanic maps
  to a PX Goal, no undocumented edge cases. Is that right?"
- **World → Scope.** "World and narrative in place. Confirm: world rules are
  design rules, every story beat maps to a mechanic. Ready to price this?"
- **Scope → /gdd g1.** "Before I compile: anything decided in conversation but
  not written into a section yet? Those are the hidden open questions that
  break documents."

## Walker context

The engine is Godot unless the project pins another. Mechanics are written so
they can be implemented and tested in Godot: scene owner, node types, input
action names, signals, collision layers. Mark a path `proposed` until it exists.
Separate source observation, proposed design, approved design, implemented
behavior, and verified behavior; the `/gdd reverse` tags make this explicit.
Producing a GDD is not producing a game, and a newer GDD does not validate an
older build.

Start every fresh session, and `/gdd` with no arguments, with the Welcome Menu:
the persona line, the two modes, the argument grammar, and the command table
generated from `commands.yaml`.

# the phase-gate check. One entry per command; aliases resolve to the id.
# Design commands: 30 · Walker additions: 5 · Navigation: 3

phases:
  vision: Vision
  systems: Systems
  world: World
  scope: Scope
  build: Build
  refine: Refinement
  walker: Walker additions
  nav: Navigation

gates:
  vision: {signed_after: v4, required_by: [s1, s2, s3, s4]}
  systems: {signed_after: s4, required_by: [w1, w2, w3]}
  world: {signed_after: w3, required_by: [p1, p2, p3, p4]}
  scope: {signed_after: p4, required_by: [g1, tasks]}

commands:
  - id: v1
    aliases: [intake]
    phase: vision
    gate: none
    output: "design/GAME-BRIEF.md"
    spec: commands/v1.md
    summary: "Vision intake. Nine questions, one at a time (interactive) or answered from the"
  - id: v2
    aliases: [pillars]
    phase: vision
    gate: none
    output: "design/sections/03-pillars.md"
    spec: commands/v2.md
    summary: "3\u20134 design pillars. For each: name (2\u20134 words), player experience it protects,"
  - id: v3
    aliases: [loop]
    phase: vision
    gate: none
    output: "design/sections/04-loop.md"
    spec: commands/v3.md
    summary: "Core loop at three scales"

# /gdd reverse

Phase: Walker additions · Aliases: `/gdd excavate`, `/gdd fromcode`, `/gdd recover` · Gate required: none
Output: `design/GDD.md (+ IMPLEMENTATION-MAP.md, decisions.md)`

Reverse-engineer a GDD from an existing codebase. Zelda's original kit does not
have this; Walker needs it because most of its games start as recovered code.

Argument: `--path <dir>` (default: project root). Optional `--engine` override.

PASS 1 — INVENTORY (read only, no design opinions yet)
  Detect engine: `project.godot`, `Cargo.toml` with bevy, `package.json` with
  babylonjs, `Assets/` + `ProjectSettings/` (Unity). Then collect:
  - scenes / prefabs and their root node types
  - scripts and the classes, exported vars, signals they declare
  - input actions (`[input]` in project.godot or equivalent), collision layers
  - resources, save/load code, scene-transition code
  - assets by category with counts and maturity guess (L0–L4)
  - README, docs, comments, TODOs, and `git log --oneline` for design history
  Write `design/IMPLEMENTATION-MAP.md`: one row per discovered feature with its
  actual scene/script paths and line references.

PASS 2 — RECONSTRUCTION
  Fill the sixteen GDD sections from the inventory. Every claim carries one tag:
  - `[OBSERVED path:line]` the code does this
  - `[INFERRED]` the code strongly implies this; state the evidence
  - `[MISSING]` the code cannot tell you this (intent, PX Goals, target player,
    pillars almost always land here)
  Sprites do not prove a mechanic; a script without a scene does not prove a
  working feature; a TODO is not a design decision. Never invent lore.
  Numbers found in code (speeds, timers, HP) are recorded as `[OBSERVED]` tuning
  values, not as approved design.

PASS 3 — ZELDA'S READ
  Run the 7 Failure Mode audit on the recovered document. Ghost Center and
  Mechanic Mirage are expected; say what the code's structure suggests the
  vision was, marked `[INFERRED]`. Every `[MISSING]` item becomes an open
  question in `design/decisions.md` with the stakes of leaving it unanswered.
  Interactive: then run the subset of intake questions the code could not
  answer, one at a time. Silent: leave them open.

PASS 4 — VISUALS
  Apply the visuals contract from `commands/deck.md`: embed the project's own
  captures and design art where they are the evidence, draw the recovered state
  machine and level flow as SVG in `design/diagrams/`, and write `design/DECK.html`
  for the review.

`design/DESIGN-STATUS.json` gets `"mode": "recovered"` and all gates unsigned.
A recovered GDD describes what exists; it is not an approval of any of it.

## Contract

- Read `persona.md`, then the project's `design/` folder (brief, sections, decisions,
  DESIGN-STATUS.json) before writing. Preserve human edits in existing files.
- Interactive: if the gate above is unsigned, ask the gate question first and stop.
  Silent (`silent` flag): proceed, and record "gate — unsigned at time of
  writing" in the output header.
- Write the output file; in chat give what changed, the assumptions made, and the
  next command. Long content never goes to chat.
- Bump `revision` in `design/DESIGN-STATUS.json` when a section changes.

actually implements and verify that behavior; do not invent new mechanics for

development teardown alternating exact code with actual visible output.

# walker-3d-platformer — current-build design document

This describes the inspected official-demo adaptation, not a claim that a new
game was generated from scratch. The initial Walker change is the project name.

## Playable idea

A blue robot moves through a textured 3D platform environment, jumps between
surfaces, collects coins and shoots projectiles at patrolling enemies. A camera
follows the character and responds to obstructing geometry. There is no inspected
top-level game script establishing a scored win/ending; do not invent one.

## Mechanisms in the source

- Player: CharacterBody3D, camera-relative input, ground acceleration and turning,
  limited air steering, gravity, held/released jump height, animation blending.
- Recovery: reset action or falling below y=-12 restores initial position and
  clears velocity using the implemented controller; this is not a driver shortcut.
- Shooting: press-edge spawns a Bullet rigid body at the character's muzzle,
  sets its initial velocity, excludes player collision and plays the shot sound.
- Coins: Area3D accepts Player contact once, increments coins and plays take
  animation; the player updates a layered Label3D counter.
- Enemies: floor/wall rays govern patrol/turning. Enabled bullet contact triggers
  dying state, impact/explosion animation and sound, then removal.
- World/art: saved scenes, imported robot models, tiled terrain/resources,
  materials, lighting, particles and original sound assets. Preserve attribution.
- Camera: follow distance/height constraints, obstruction rays and autoturn.
- Touch controls: touchscreen-dependent UI and virtual joystick action mapping;
  actual touchscreen and gamepad hardware operation remains unverified.

## Verification to date

Four normal-input assertions pass: movement, jump, projectile creation, reset.
Feature-route03 observes two coins collected and an enemy hit without writing
gameplay state. These headless assertions alone are not film evidence or human
playtesting. Real route capture and event inspection remain required.

## Human and AI responsibilities

AI reads source, chooses normal inputs, records evidence, explains code/output,
and logs failed attempts. People judge responsiveness, accessibility, difficulty
and fun. One bounded improvement at a time; a failed prediction belongs in the
Frictional log. Neither a passing test nor a polished explainer establishes fun.

## Film contract

Two independent Liam/Walker films: implemented-feature walkthrough, then
code→visible-result teardown. Every excerpt immediately precedes actual output.
Native4K with original-speed gameplay and deliberate original-sound mix, no
burned captions, standard outro only. No publication implied by local completion.

1	class_name Player
2	extends CharacterBody3D
3	
4	enum _Anim {
5		FLOOR,
6		AIR,
7	}
8	
9	const SHOOT_TIME: float = 1.5
10	const SHOOT_SCALE: float = 2.0
11	const CHAR_SCALE := Vector3(0.3, 0.3, 0.3)
12	const MAX_SPEED: float = 6.0
13	const TURN_SPEED: float = 40.0
14	const JUMP_VELOCITY: float = 12.5
15	const BULLET_SPEED: float = 20.0
16	const AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL: bool = false
17	const ACCEL: float = 14.0
18	const DEACCEL: float = 14.0
19	const AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR: float = 0.5
20	const SHARP_TURN_THRESHOLD: float = deg_to_rad(140.0)
21	
22	var movement_dir := Vector3()
23	var jumping: bool = false
24	var prev_shoot: bool = false
25	var shoot_blend: float = 0.0
26	
27	# Number of coins collected.
28	var coins: int = 0
29	
30	@onready var initial_position := position
31	@onready var _camera := $Target/Camera3D as Camera3D
32	@onready var _animation_tree := $AnimationTree as AnimationTree
33	
34	
35	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
36		if Input.is_action_pressed(&"reset_position") or global_position.y < -12:
37			# Player hit the reset button or fell off the map.
38			position = initial_position
39			velocity = Vector3.ZERO
40			# We teleported the player on the lines above. Reset interpolation
41			# to prevent it from interpolating from the old player position
42			# to the new position.
43			reset_physics_interpolation()
44	
45		# Update coin count and its "parallax" copies.
46		# This gives text a pseudo-3D appearance while still using Label3D instead of the more limited TextMesh.
47		%CoinCount.text = str(coins)
48		%CoinCount.get_node(^"Parallax").text = str(coins)
49		%CoinCount.get_node(^"Parallax2").text = str(coins)
50		%CoinCount.get_node(^"Parallax3").text = str(coins)
51		%CoinCount.get_node(^"Parallax4").text = str(coins)
52	
53		velocity += get_gravity() * delta
54	
55		var anim := _Anim.FLOOR
56	
57		var vertical_velocity := velocity.y
58		var horizontal_velocity := Vector3(velocity.x, 0, velocity.z)
59	
60		var horizontal_direction := horizontal_velocity.normalized()
61		var horizontal_speed := horizontal_velocity.length()
62	
63		# Player input.
64		var cam_basis := _camera.get_global_transform().basis
65		var movement_vec2 := Input.get_vector(&"move_left", &"move_right", &"move_forward", &"move_back")
66		var movement_direction := cam_basis * Vector3(movement_vec2.x, 0, movement_vec2.y)
67		movement_direction.y = 0
68		movement_direction = movement_direction.normalized()
69	
70		var jump_attempt := Input.is_action_pressed(&"jump")
71	
72		if is_on_floor():
73			var sharp_turn := horizontal_speed > 0.1 and \
74					acos(movement_direction.dot(horizontal_direction)) > SHARP_TURN_THRESHOLD
75	
76			if movement_direction.length() > 0.1 and not sharp_turn:
77				if horizontal_speed > 0.001:
78					horizontal_direction = adjust_facing(
79							horizontal_direction,
80							movement_direction,
81							delta,
82							1.0 / horizontal_speed * TURN_SPEED,
83							Vector3.UP
84						)
85				else:
86					horizontal_direction = movement_direction
87	
88				if horizontal_speed < MAX_SPEED:
89					horizontal_speed += ACCEL * delta
90			else:
91				horizontal_speed -= DEACCEL * delta
92				if horizontal_speed < 0:
93					horizontal_speed = 0
94	
95			horizontal_velocity = horizontal_direction * horizontal_speed
96	
97			var mesh_xform := ($Player/Skeleton as Node3D).get_transform()
98			var facing_mesh := -mesh_xform.basis[0].normalized()
99			facing_mesh = (facing_mesh - Vector3.UP * facing_mesh.dot(Vector3.UP)).normalized()
100	
101			if horizontal_speed > 0:
102				facing_mesh = adjust_facing(
103						facing_mesh,
104						movement_direction,
105						delta,
106						1.0 / horizontal_speed * TURN_SPEED,
107						Vector3.UP
108					)
109			var m3 := Basis(
110					-facing_mesh,
111					Vector3.UP,
112					-facing_mesh.cross(Vector3.UP).normalized()
113				).scaled(CHAR_SCALE)
114	
115			$Player/Skeleton.set_transform(Transform3D(m3, mesh_xform.origin))
116	
117			if not jumping and jump_attempt:
118				vertical_velocity = JUMP_VELOCITY
119				jumping = true
120				$SoundJump.play()
121	
122		else:
123			anim = _Anim.AIR
124	
125			if movement_direction.length() > 0.1:
126				horizontal_velocity += movement_direction * (ACCEL * AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR * delta)
127				if horizontal_velocity.length() > MAX_SPEED:
128					horizontal_velocity = horizontal_velocity.normalized() * MAX_SPEED
129			elif AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL:
130				horizontal_speed = horizontal_speed - (DEACCEL * AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR * delta)
131				if horizontal_speed < 0:
132					horizontal_speed = 0
133				horizontal_velocity = horizontal_direction * horizontal_speed
134	
135			if Input.is_action_just_released(&"jump") and velocity.y > 0.0:
136				# Reduce jump height if releasing the jump key before reaching the apex.
137				vertical_velocity *= 0.7
138	
139		if jumping and vertical_velocity < 0:
140			jumping = false
141	
142		velocity = horizontal_velocity + Vector3.UP * vertical_velocity
143	
144		if is_on_floor():
145			movement_dir = velocity
146	
147		move_and_slide()
148	
149		if shoot_blend > 0:
150			shoot_blend *= 0.97
151			if (shoot_blend < 0):
152				shoot_blend = 0
153		var shoot_attempt := Input.is_action_pressed(&"shoot")
154		if shoot_attempt and not prev_shoot:
155			shoot_blend = SHOOT_TIME
156			var bullet := preload("res://player/bullet/bullet.tscn").instantiate() as Bullet
157			bullet.set_transform($Player/Skeleton/Bullet.get_global_transform().orthonormalized())
158			get_parent().add_child(bullet)
159			bullet.set_linear_velocity(
160					$Player/Skeleton/Bullet.get_global_transform().basis[2].normalized() * BULLET_SPEED
161				)
162			bullet.add_collision_exception_with(self)
163			$SoundShoot.play()
164	
165		prev_shoot = shoot_attempt
166	
167		if is_on_floor():
168			# How much the player should be blending between the "idle" and "walk/run" animations.
169			_animation_tree[&"parameters/run/blend_amount"] = horizontal_speed / MAX_SPEED
170	
171			# How much the player should be running (as opposed to walking). 0.0 = fully walking, 1.0 = fully running.
172			_animation_tree[&"parameters/speed/blend_amount"] = minf(1.0, horizontal_speed / (MAX_SPEED * 0.5))
173	
174		_animation_tree[&"parameters/state/blend_amount"] = anim
175		_animation_tree[&"parameters/air_dir/blend_amount"] = clampf(-velocity.y / 4 + 0.5, 0, 1)
176		_animation_tree[&"parameters/gun/blend_amount"] = minf(shoot_blend, 1.0)
177	
178	
179	func adjust_facing(facing: Vector3, target: Vector3, step: float, adjust_rate: float, \
180			current_gn: Vector3) -> Vector3:
181		var normal := target
182		var t := normal.cross(current_gn).normalized()
183	
184		var x := normal.dot(facing)
185		var y := t.dot(facing)
186	
187		var ang := atan2(y,x)
188	
189		if absf(ang) < 0.001:
190			return facing
191	
192		var s := signf(ang)
193		ang = ang * s
194		var turn := ang * adjust_rate * step
195		var a: float
196		if ang < turn:
197			a = ang
198		else:
199			a = turn
200		ang = (ang - a) * s
201	
202		return (normal * cos(ang) + t * sin(ang)) * facing.length()

4	const MAX_HEIGHT = 2.0
5	const MIN_HEIGHT = 0.0
6	
7	var collision_exception: Array[RID] = []
8	
9	@export var min_distance: float = 0.5
10	@export var max_distance: float = 3.5
11	@export var angle_v_adjust: float = 0.0
12	@export var autoturn_ray_aperture: float = 25.0
13	@export var autoturn_speed: float = 50.0
14	
15	
16	func _ready() -> void:
17		# Find collision exceptions for ray.
18		# This is done to prevent the player and enemies from colliding
19		# with the camera.
20		var node: Node = self
21		while is_instance_valid(node):
22			if node is RigidBody3D or node is CharacterBody3D:
23				collision_exception.append(node.get_rid())
24				break
25			else:
26				node = node.get_parent()
27	
28		# This detaches the camera transform from the parent spatial node.
29		set_as_top_level(true)
30	
31	
32	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
33		var target := (get_parent() as Node3D).get_global_transform().origin
34		var pos := get_global_transform().origin
35	
36		var difference := pos - target
37	
38		# Regular delta follow.
39	
40		# Check ranges.
41		if difference.length() < min_distance:
42			difference = difference.normalized() * min_distance
43		elif  difference.length() > max_distance:
44			difference = difference.normalized() * max_distance
45	
46		# Check upper and lower height.
47		difference.y = clamp(difference.y, MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_HEIGHT)
48	
49		# Check autoturn.
50		var ds := PhysicsServer3D.space_get_direct_state(get_world_3d().get_space())
51	
52		var col_left := ds.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(
53				target,
54				target + Basis(Vector3.UP, deg_to_rad(autoturn_ray_aperture)) * (difference),
55				0xffffffff,
56				collision_exception
57			))
58		var col := ds.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(
59				target,
60				target + difference,
61				0xffffffff,
62				collision_exception
63			))
64		var col_right := ds.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(
65				target,
66				target + Basis(Vector3.UP, deg_to_rad(-autoturn_ray_aperture)) * (difference),
67				0xffffffff,
68				collision_exception
69			))
70	
71		if not col.is_empty():
72			# If main ray was occluded, get camera closer, this is the worst case scenario.
73			difference = col.position - target
74		elif not col_left.is_empty() and col_right.is_empty():
75			# If only left ray is occluded, turn the camera around to the right.
76			difference = Basis(Vector3.UP, deg_to_rad(-delta * (autoturn_speed))) * difference
77		elif col_left.is_empty() and not col_right.is_empty():
78			# If only right ray is occluded, turn the camera around to the left.
79			difference = Basis(Vector3.UP, deg_to_rad(delta * autoturn_speed)) * difference
80		# Do nothing otherwise, left and right are occluded but center is not, so do not autoturn.
81	
82		# Apply lookat.
83		if difference.is_zero_approx():
84			difference = (pos - target).normalized() * 0.0001
85	
86		pos = target + difference
87	
88		look_at_from_position(pos, target, Vector3.UP)
89	
90		# Turn a little up or down.
91		transform.basis = Basis(transform.basis[0], deg_to_rad(angle_v_adjust)) * transform.basis

1	extends RigidBody3D
2	
3	
4	const ACCEL: float = 5.0
5	const DEACCEL: float = 20.0
6	const MAX_SPEED: float = 2.0
7	const ROT_SPEED: float = 1.0
8	
9	var prev_advance: bool = false
10	var dying: bool = false
11	var rot_dir: float = 4.0
12	
13	@onready var _animation_player := $Enemy/AnimationPlayer as AnimationPlayer
14	@onready var _ray_floor := $Enemy/Skeleton/RayFloor as RayCast3D
15	@onready var _ray_wall := $Enemy/Skeleton/RayWall as RayCast3D
16	
17	
18	func _integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState3D) -> void:
19		var delta := state.get_step()
20		var lin_velocity := state.get_linear_velocity()
21	
22	 	# Apply gravity.
23		lin_velocity += get_gravity() * delta
24		var up := -get_gravity().normalized()
25	
26		if dying:
27			state.set_linear_velocity(lin_velocity)
28			return
29	
30		for i in state.get_contact_count():
31			var contact_collider := state.get_contact_collider_object(i)
32			var contact_normal := state.get_contact_local_normal(i)
33	
34			if is_instance_valid(contact_collider):
35				if contact_collider is Bullet and contact_collider.enabled:
36					dying = true
37					axis_lock_angular_x = false
38					axis_lock_angular_y = false
39					axis_lock_angular_z = false
40					collision_layer = 0
41					state.set_angular_velocity(-contact_normal.cross(up).normalized() * 33.0)
42					_animation_player.play(&"impact")
43					_animation_player.queue(&"extra/explode")
44					contact_collider.enabled = false
45					$SoundWalkLoop.stop()
46					$SoundHit.play()
47					return
48	
49		var advance: bool = _ray_floor.is_colliding() and not _ray_wall.is_colliding()
50	
51		var dir: Vector3 = ($Enemy/Skeleton as Node3D).get_transform().basis.z.normalized()
52		var deaccel_dir: Vector3 = dir
53	
54		if advance:
55			if dir.dot(lin_velocity) < MAX_SPEED:
56				lin_velocity += dir * ACCEL * delta
57			deaccel_dir = dir.cross(get_gravity()).normalized()
58		else:
59			if prev_advance:
60				rot_dir = 1
61	
62			dir = Basis(up, rot_dir * ROT_SPEED * (delta)) * dir
63			$Enemy/Skeleton.set_transform(Transform3D().looking_at(-dir, up))
64	
65		var dspeed: float = deaccel_dir.dot(lin_velocity)
66		dspeed -= DEACCEL * delta
67		if dspeed < 0:
68			dspeed = 0
69	
70		lin_velocity = lin_velocity - deaccel_dir * deaccel_dir.dot(lin_velocity) \
71				+ deaccel_dir * dspeed
72	
73		state.set_linear_velocity(lin_velocity)
74		prev_advance = advance
75	
76	
77	func _die() -> void:
78		queue_free()
79

func _on_coin_body_enter(body: Node) -> void:

		$Animation.play(&"take")
		taken = true

		# As a result, we can safely increment its `coins` property.
		body.coins += 1

func _ready() -> void:

		var new_light: DirectionalLight3D = $DirectionalLight3D.duplicate()
		new_light.light_energy = 0.25
		new_light.sky_mode = DirectionalLight3D.SKY_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY
		add_child(new_light)

1	class_name VirtualJoystickAddon
2	extends Control
3	
4	## A simple virtual joystick for touchscreens, with useful options.
5	## Github: https://github.com/MarcoFazioRandom/Virtual-Joystick-Godot
6	
7	# EXPORTED VARIABLES
8	
9	## The color of the button when the joystick is pressed.
10	@export var pressed_color := Color.GRAY
11	
12	## If the input is inside this range, the output is zero.
13	@export_range(0, 200, 1) var deadzone_size: float = 10.0
14	
15	## The max distance the tip can reach.
16	@export_range(0, 500, 1) var clampzone_size: float = 75.0
17	
18	enum Joystick_mode {
19		FIXED, ## The joystick doesn't move.
20		DYNAMIC, ## Every time the joystick area is pressed, the joystick position is set on the touched position.
21		FOLLOWING, ## When the finger moves outside the joystick area, the joystick will follow it.
22	}
23	
24	## If the joystick stays in the same position or appears on the touched position when touch is started.
25	@export var joystick_mode := Joystick_mode.FIXED
26	
27	enum Visibility_mode {
28		ALWAYS, ## Always visible.
29		TOUCHSCREEN_ONLY, ## Visible on touch screens only.
30		WHEN_TOUCHED, ## Visible only when touched.
31	}
32	
33	## If the joystick is always visible, or is shown only if there is a touchscreen.
34	@export var visibility_mode := Visibility_mode.ALWAYS
35	
36	## If true, the joystick uses Input Actions. (Project -> Project Settings -> Input Map)
37	@export var use_input_actions: bool = true
38	
39	@export var action_left: String = "move_left"
40	@export var action_right: String = "move_right"
41	@export var action_up: String = "move_forward"
42	@export var action_down: String = "move_back"
43	
44	# PUBLIC VARIABLES
45	
46	## If the joystick is receiving inputs.
47	var is_pressed: bool = false
48	
49	# The joystick output.
50	var output := Vector2.ZERO
51	
52	# PRIVATE VARIABLES
53	
54	var _touch_index: int = -1
55	
56	@onready var _base: TextureRect = $Base
57	@onready var _tip: TextureRect = $Base/Tip
58	
59	@onready var _base_default_position: Vector2 = _base.position
60	@onready var _tip_default_position: Vector2 = _tip.position
61	
62	@onready var _default_color : Color = _tip.modulate
63	
64	# FUNCTIONS
65	
66	func _ready() -> void:
67		if not DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available():
68			hide()
69	
70		if visibility_mode == Visibility_mode.WHEN_TOUCHED:
71			hide()
72	
73	
74	func _input(input_event: InputEvent) -> void:
75		if input_event is InputEventScreenTouch:
76			if input_event.pressed:
77				if _is_point_inside_joystick_area(input_event.position) and _touch_index == -1:
78					if joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.DYNAMIC or joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.FOLLOWING or (
79							joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.FIXED and _is_point_inside_base(input_event.position)):
80						if joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.DYNAMIC or joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.FOLLOWING:
81							_move_base(input_event.position)
82						if visibility_mode == Visibility_mode.WHEN_TOUCHED:
83							show()
84						_touch_index = input_event.index
85						_tip.modulate = pressed_color
86						_update_joystick(input_event.position)
87						get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
88			elif input_event.index == _touch_index:
89				_reset()
90				if visibility_mode == Visibility_mode.WHEN_TOUCHED:
91					hide()
92				get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
93		elif input_event is InputEventScreenDrag:
94			if input_event.index == _touch_index:
95				_update_joystick(input_event.position)
96				get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
97	
98	
99	func _move_base(new_position: Vector2) -> void:
100		_base.global_position = new_position - _base.pivot_offset * get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale()
101	
102	
103	func _move_tip(new_position: Vector2) -> void:
104		_tip.global_position = new_position - _tip.pivot_offset * _base.get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale()
105	
106	
107	func _is_point_inside_joystick_area(point: Vector2) -> bool:
108		var x: bool = point.x >= global_position.x and point.x <= global_position.x + (size.x * get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale().x)
109		var y: bool = point.y >= global_position.y and point.y <= global_position.y + (size.y * get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale().y)
110		return x and y
111	
112	
113	func _get_base_radius() -> Vector2:
114		return _base.size * _base.get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale() / 2.0
115	
116	
117	func _is_point_inside_base(point: Vector2) -> bool:
118		var base_radius: Vector2 = _get_base_radius()
119		var center: Vector2 = _base.global_position + base_radius
120		var vector: Vector2 = point - center
121		return vector.length_squared() <= base_radius.x * base_radius.x
122	
123	
124	func _update_joystick(touch_position: Vector2) -> void:
125		var base_radius: Vector2 = _get_base_radius()
126		var center: Vector2 = _base.global_position + base_radius
127		var vector: Vector2 = touch_position - center
128		vector = vector.limit_length(clampzone_size)
129	
130		if joystick_mode == Joystick_mode.FOLLOWING and touch_position.distance_to(center) > clampzone_size:
131			_move_base(touch_position - vector)
132	
133		_move_tip(center + vector)
134	
135		if vector.length_squared() > deadzone_size * deadzone_size:
136			is_pressed = true
137			output = (vector - (vector.normalized() * deadzone_size)) / (clampzone_size - deadzone_size)
138		else:
139			is_pressed = false
140			output = Vector2.ZERO
141	
142		if use_input_actions:
143			# Release actions.
144			if output.x >= 0.0 and Input.is_action_pressed(action_left):
145				Input.action_release(action_left)
146			if output.x <= 0.0 and Input.is_action_pressed(action_right):
147				Input.action_release(action_right)
148			if output.y >= 0.0 and Input.is_action_pressed(action_up):
149				Input.action_release(action_up)
150			if output.y <= 0.0 and Input.is_action_pressed(action_down):
151				Input.action_release(action_down)
152	
153			# Press actions.
154			if output.x < 0.0:
155				Input.action_press(action_left, -output.x)
156			if output.x > 0.0:
157				Input.action_press(action_right, output.x)
158			if output.y < 0.0:
159				Input.action_press(action_up, -output.y)
160			if output.y > 0.0:
161				Input.action_press(action_down, output.y)
162	
163	
164	func _reset() -> void:
165		is_pressed = false
166		output = Vector2.ZERO
167		_touch_index = -1
168		_tip.modulate = _default_color
169		_base.position = _base_default_position
170		_tip.position = _tip_default_position
171		# Release actions.
172		if use_input_actions:
173			for action:String in [action_left, action_right, action_down, action_up]:
174				if Input.is_action_pressed(action):
175					Input.action_release(action)
176

# /gdd deck

Phase: Walker additions · Aliases: `/gdd slides` · Gate required: none
Output: `design/DECK.html (+ design/diagrams/*.svg)`

Slide deck for the current GDD, for people who review a design in a room rather
than in a file. Self-contained HTML in `design/DECK.html` (arrow keys / space to
advance, no external dependencies), one idea per slide, Zelda's register.

VISUALS CONTRACT (also binding on `draft`, `reverse`, and `g1`):
1. Use what the project already has before drawing anything: rendered game
   captures, gallery frames, existing design SVG/PNG, evidence screenshots.
   Reference them by relative path; never copy or re-encode them. Caption each
   with what it proves and its provenance (`[OBSERVED]` capture vs design art).
2. Draw the rest as SVG in `design/diagrams/`: the core loop at three scales,
   the session state machine, the level/task flow, the obstacle taxonomy, the
   feature dependency map. Every diagram carries a title, a one-line desc, and
   the IDs it references (M-xx, S-xx, F-xx). Same palette as the game.
3. Everything that is neither existing art nor a diagram is a text slide:
   vision, pillars, PX Goals, CORE percentage, top 3 risks, open questions.
4. A slide that repeats a paragraph of the GDD is wrong. Slides carry the
   claim; the GDD carries the argument. Link each slide to its section.
5. Mark proposed elements dashed and observed elements solid, in diagrams and
   in slides alike, so a viewer can see what exists without reading the tags.

## Contract

- Read `persona.md`, then the project's `design/` folder (brief, sections, decisions,
  DESIGN-STATUS.json) before writing. Preserve human edits in existing files.
- Interactive: if the gate above is unsigned, ask the gate question first and stop.
  Silent (`silent` flag): proceed, and record "gate — unsigned at time of
  writing" in the output header.
- Write the output file; in chat give what changed, the assumptions made, and the
  next command. Long content never goes to chat.
- Bump `revision` in `design/DESIGN-STATUS.json` when a section changes.

Sharp turns above 140° halt acceleration briefly, turning happens at 40°/s scaled by speed, and air control gives half the ground acceleration with no deceleration while airborne. # Game Design Document — walker-3d-platformer

**Recovered** by `/gdd reverse --path godot` · 2026-09-27  
**Gate — unsigned at time of writing (silent flag)**  
**Revision:** 1 · **Mode:** recovered  

Every claim carries an evidence tag:  
- `[OBSERVED path:line]` — the code does this  
- `[INFERRED]` — the code strongly implies this; evidence stated  
- `[MISSING]` — the code cannot tell you this  

Numbers found in code are `[OBSERVED]` tuning values, not approved design. A recovered GDD describes what exists; it is not an approval of any of it.

---

## 01. METADATA

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Game ID | walker-3d-platformer |
| Engine | Godot 4.7 `[OBSERVED godot/project.godot:18]` |
| Physics | Jolt Physics 3D, 120 Hz, interpolated `[OBSERVED godot/project.godot:149-151]` |
| Renderer | Forward+ (default); gl_compatibility (fallback) `[OBSERVED godot/stage/stage.gd:4]` |
| Gravity | 22.0 m/s² `[OBSERVED godot/project.godot:153]` |
| Main scene | res://game.tscn `[OBSERVED godot/project.godot:17]` |
| Scripts | 8 GDScript files (typed) `[OBSERVED]` |
| Scenes | 8 .tscn files `[OBSERVED]` |
| GLB models | 2 (player.glb, enemy.glb) `[OBSERVED]` |
| GDD revision | 1 |
| Recovered | 2026-09-27 |

---

## 02. VISION SUMMARY

**Logline:** `[MISSING]`

**Playable idea** `[OBSERVED godot/GAME-BRIEF.md]`: A blue robot moves through a textured 3D platform environment, jumps between surfaces, collects coins, and shoots projectiles at patrolling enemies. A camera follows the character and responds to obstructing geometry.

**Walker context** `[OBSERVED godot/GAME-BRIEF.md]`: This is a Walker adaptation of Godot's official 3D Platformer demo. The initial change is the project name only. Controls, movement, scenes, art, and sound are preserved from the upstream Godot official demo (tagged `3d`, `demo`, `gridmap`, `official`, `physics`).

**Teaching intent** `[INFERRED from GAME-BRIEF.md]`: The project demonstrates CharacterBody3D 3D movement, camera following with obstruction handling, coin collectibles, and enemy patrol — observable and inspectable by students of the Godot engine. The teaching loop is: Game brief → Build → Playtest → Inspect → Revise → Export.

**No top-level game script establishing a scored win/ending is observed** `[OBSERVED godot/GAME-BRIEF.md]`. Do not invent one.

---

## 03. DESIGN PILLARS

`[MISSING]` No explicit design pillars are documented in any source file.

Zelda's read — pillars inferred from code structure and the Walker brief. These require human confirmation before any design decision references them.

**Pillar A — Grounded Physical Movement**  
*Player experience it protects:* The character must feel like it has mass and respond to momentum.  
*Evidence:* Jolt Physics at 120 Hz; gravity=22.0 m/s² (2.24× Earth); AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL=false (no air stopping); AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR=0.5 (limited air authority); sharp-turn threshold at 140° breaks momentum. The character decelerates into a direction change rather than snapping. `[INFERRED from player.gd constants]`  
*What violates it:* instant-stop air movement, floaty gravity, unrestricted air steering.

**Pillar B — Readable Camera**  
*Player experience it protects:* The player sees what matters without fighting the camera.  
*Evidence:* Three-ray autoturn system pushes camera away from geometry before it clips. Obstruction pull moves camera to collision point as worst case. Top-level detach prevents parenting artifacts. Height clamped [0, 2] prevents floor-skating view. `[INFERRED from follow_camera.gd]`  
*What violates it:* camera clipping into geometry, manual camera rotation added without autoturn integration.

**Pillar C — Inspectability**  
*Player experience it protects (for the Walker/learning audience):* Every mechanism is readable from source.  
*Evidence:* 8 scripts, no AutoLoads, no scene-specific game manager, all feature logic self-contained in owning scene scripts. `[INFERRED from GAME-BRIEF.md and codebase structure]`  
*What violates it:* global state, singletons that hide flow, cross-scene coupling.

---

## 04. CORE LOOP

Diagrams: `design/diagrams/core-loop.svg`

**Micro loop (5–15 seconds)** `[INFERRED from mechanics]`  
Move → Orient via camera → Jump to platform → Shoot enemy OR collect coin → Land → Move  
Reset available at any point (R or fall).

**Macro loop (30–120 seconds)** `[INFERRED from level layout]`  
Start at spawn → Navigate coin cluster → Collect coins (Area3D feedback) → Locate nearby enemy → Shoot (press-edge) → Proceed to next area of the level

**Session loop** `[MISSING win state]`  
Start at spawn → Explore open level → [Fall → auto-reset to spawn] → [No session end observed]  
The session has no designed end state. This is a confirmed gap, not a feature. See OQ-01 in decisions.md.

---

## 05. PLAYER EXPERIENCE GOALS

`[MISSING]` No PX Goals are documented in any source file.

Zelda's read — inferred from the mechanics as built. All require human confirmation.

| ID | PX Goal | Evidence basis |
|---|---|---|
| PX-01 | Feel the weight of a grounded character — momentum builds and costs something to redirect | ACCEL=14, gravity=22, sharp-turn stop, air factor=0.5 `[INFERRED player.gd]` |
| PX-02 | Read the 3D space through a camera that works for you, not against you | Three-ray autoturn, obstruction pull, height clamp `[INFERRED follow_camera.gd]` |
| PX-03 | Control jump height deliberately — hold for distance, cut for precision | Variable jump: JUMP_VELOCITY=12.5, cut×0.7; measured heights 1.53m/3.60m `[INFERRED player.gd, evidence/]` |
| PX-04 | Use coin clusters as breadcrumbs through unfamiliar 3D space | 73 coins in 6–8 clusters across level `[INFERRED game.tscn]` |
| PX-05 | Eliminate a patrolling enemy with a single well-timed shot | One-hit kill: bullet contact → enemy queue_free `[INFERRED enemy.gd]` |

---

## 06. MECHANICS

Diagrams: `design/diagrams/player-state-machine.svg`, `design/diagrams/enemy-patrol.svg`

---

### M-01 — Ground Movement
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd`  
**Node:** CharacterBody3D (class Player)  
**Input actions:** `move_forward` (W/↑/LStick-Y-), `move_back` (S/↓/LStick-Y+), `move_left` (A/←/LStick-X-), `move_right` (D/→/LStick-X+)

Camera-relative horizontal movement. `Input.get_vector()` produces a 2D input; it is rotated into the camera's basis then projected onto the XZ plane (Y zeroed, renormalized). Separate `horizontal_direction` and `horizontal_speed` allow smooth arc turning via `adjust_facing()`.

Sharp turn detection: if moving speed >0.1 and angle between movement direction and current heading >140°, acceleration is suppressed. The player must decelerate before reversing direction. `[OBSERVED player.gd:73-74]`

Mesh rotation uses `adjust_facing()` — angular interpolation toward movement direction, rate weighted by `TURN_SPEED / speed`. `[OBSERVED player.gd:97-115, 179-202]`

| Constant | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| MAX_SPEED | 6.0 m/s | `[OBSERVED player.gd:14]` |
| ACCEL | 14.0 m/s² | `[OBSERVED player.gd:18]` |
| DEACCEL | 14.0 m/s² | `[OBSERVED player.gd:19]` |
| TURN_SPEED | 40.0 | `[OBSERVED player.gd:13]` |
| SHARP_TURN_THRESHOLD | deg_to_rad(140°) | `[OBSERVED player.gd:21]` |
| CHAR_SCALE | Vector3(0.3, 0.3, 0.3) | `[OBSERVED player.gd:12]` |

---

### M-02 — Air Movement
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd:122-133`

In air, horizontal acceleration is capped at `AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR × ACCEL`. No air deceleration when no input (`AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL = false` — constant, not tunable at runtime). Air max speed capped at `MAX_SPEED`. `[OBSERVED player.gd:122-133]`

| Constant | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR | 0.5 | `[OBSERVED player.gd:20]` |
| AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL | false | `[OBSERVED player.gd:17]` |

---

### M-03 — Variable Jump
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd:117-137`  
**Input action:** `jump` (Space / Mouse RMB / Gamepad A)

Jump initiates only when `is_on_floor()` is true and `jumping` flag is false. Sets `vertical_velocity = JUMP_VELOCITY`, sets `jumping = true`, plays SoundJump. Releasing jump before apex while `velocity.y > 0` multiplies vertical velocity by 0.7. `jumping` flag clears when `vertical_velocity < 0` (past apex). Single jump only — no coyote time, no double jump observed.

| Constant | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| JUMP_VELOCITY | 12.5 m/s | `[OBSERVED player.gd:15]` |
| Early-release multiplier | 0.7 | `[OBSERVED player.gd:137]` |
| Measured rise (6-tick hold) | ~1.53 m | `[OBSERVED evidence/baseline-probe.json]` |
| Measured rise (60-tick hold) | ~3.60 m | `[OBSERVED evidence/baseline-probe.json]` |

---

### M-04 — Gravity
**Owner:** project.godot, CharacterBody3D  

`get_gravity()` returns the project gravity setting (22.0 m/s²) — approximately 2.24× Earth standard. Applied every `_physics_process` frame before horizontal velocity resolution. Produces faster falls and tighter arc apexes than standard Earth gravity. Physics runs at 120 Hz with interpolation enabled. `[OBSERVED godot/project.godot:149-153]`

| Setting | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Gravity | 22.0 m/s² | `[OBSERVED project.godot:153]` |
| Physics Hz | 120 | `[OBSERVED project.godot:149]` |
| Physics interpolation | true | `[OBSERVED project.godot:151]` |

---

### M-05 — Fall Recovery
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd:36-43`  
**Input action:** `reset_position` (R / Gamepad Y)

Two triggers: (1) `global_position.y < -12`, or (2) `Input.is_action_pressed("reset_position")`. Both paths: `position = initial_position` (cached in `_ready()`), `velocity = Vector3.ZERO`, `reset_physics_interpolation()` (prevents lerp from old to new position). `[OBSERVED player.gd:36-43]`

Fall threshold: y = -12. `[OBSERVED player.gd:36]`

---

### M-06 — Shooting
**Owner scenes:** `godot/player/player.tscn`, `godot/player/bullet/bullet.tscn`  
**Scripts:** `godot/player/player.gd:153-165`, `godot/player/bullet/bullet.gd`  
**Input action:** `shoot` (F9 / Mouse LMB / Gamepad B / Gamepad L3 / Gamepad Right Trigger)

Press-edge only (`shoot_attempt and not prev_shoot`). Spawns a Bullet (RigidBody3D, class Bullet) as a sibling in the scene tree via `get_parent().add_child(bullet)`. Sets bullet's global transform to the muzzle marker (`$Player/Skeleton/Bullet`) orthonormalized. Applies forward-axis velocity (`BULLET_SPEED`). Excludes player from bullet collision via `add_collision_exception_with(self)`. Plays SoundShoot. Sets `shoot_blend = SHOOT_TIME` for animation fade. `shoot_blend` decays at ×0.97 per frame. `[OBSERVED player.gd:153-165]`

`bullet.enabled = true` on spawn. Set `false` on first enemy contact to prevent multi-hit while the bullet is fading. `[OBSERVED bullet.gd:6, enemy.gd:44]`

| Constant | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| BULLET_SPEED | 20.0 m/s | `[OBSERVED player.gd:16]` |
| SHOOT_TIME | 1.5 | `[OBSERVED player.gd:9]` |
| SHOOT_SCALE | 2.0 | `[OBSERVED player.gd:10]` |

---

### M-07 — Coin Collection
**Owner scenes:** `godot/coin/coin.tscn`, `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Scripts:** `godot/coin/coin.gd`, `godot/player/player.gd:47-51`  
**Node:** Area3D

On body enter: if `body is Player` and `not taken` → play "take" animation, set `taken = true`, increment `body.coins`. One-time per instance — no respawn. `[OBSERVED coin.gd:7-13]`

Player stores count in `coins: int` (session-only, no persistence). Updates `%CoinCount` Label3D and four parallax shadow copies (`Parallax`, `Parallax2`, `Parallax3`, `Parallax4`) every physics frame for pseudo-3D depth effect. `[OBSERVED player.gd:47-51]`

73 coin instances placed in the scene in spatial clusters. `[OBSERVED game.tscn — 73 Coin nodes counted]`

---

### M-08 — Enemy Patrol
**Owner scene:** `godot/enemy/enemy.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/enemy/enemy.gd`  
**Node:** RigidBody3D

Floor ray (`_ray_floor: RayCast3D`) and wall ray (`_ray_wall: RayCast3D`) evaluated in `_integrate_forces`. `advance = _ray_floor.is_colliding() and not _ray_wall.is_colliding()`. On advance: accelerate along current facing direction; decelerate on perpendicular (lateral) axis. On not-advance: rotate in place using `Basis(up, rot_dir * ROT_SPEED * delta)`. `rot_dir` initializes to 4.0; resets to 1.0 when the enemy transitions from advance to turn (`prev_advance → false`). `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:49-73]`

### M-09 — Enemy Death
**Owner scene:** `godot/enemy/enemy.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/enemy/enemy.gd:34-47, 77-78`

Detected in `_integrate_forces` via contact loop. On contact with a Bullet where `bullet.enabled == true`: set `dying = true`, unlock all rotation axes (`axis_lock_angular_*= false`), set `collision_layer = 0` (removes from collision), apply angular spin (`-contact_normal.cross(up).normalized() * 33.0`), queue animation "impact" then "extra/explode", set `bullet.enabled = false`, stop SoundWalkLoop, play SoundHit. Returns immediately; remaining contacts ignored. `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:34-47]`

`_die()` called by animation signal (end of explode): `queue_free()`. `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:77-78]`

---

### M-10 — Follow Camera
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/follow_camera.gd`  
**Node:** Camera3D

In `_ready()`: finds ancestor RigidBody3D or CharacterBody3D and stores its RID in `collision_exception` (prevents camera rays from hitting player/enemies). Calls `set_as_top_level(true)` to decouple transform from parent. `[OBSERVED follow_camera.gd:16-29]`

In `_physics_process()`: computes `difference = cam_pos - target`. Clamps length to [min_distance, max_distance]. Clamps Y component to [MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_HEIGHT]. Casts three rays from target to `target + difference` at 0°, +autoturn_aperture°, -autoturn_aperture°. Result: center blocked → move camera to hit point; only left blocked → rotate right; only right blocked → rotate left; both sides blocked, center clear → no autoturn. Applies `look_at_from_position` then optional vertical tilt. `[OBSERVED follow_camera.gd:32-91]`

## 07. SYSTEMS

### S-01 — Movement System
**Domain:** Player locomotion  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Decouple movement authority from frame rate via physics interpolation; provide camera-relative control so 3D space feels natural.  
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Scripts:** `player.gd`, `follow_camera.gd`  
**Input actions:** `move_forward`, `move_back`, `move_left`, `move_right`, `jump`, `reset_position`  
**Core variables:** velocity (Vector3), horizontal_direction, horizontal_speed, jumping (bool), initial_position  
**Physics:** 120 Hz Jolt, interpolated `[OBSERVED project.godot:149-151]`

### S-02 — Combat System
**Domain:** Shooting and enemy elimination  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Give the player agency over moving obstacles; demonstrates RigidBody3D contact detection in `_integrate_forces`.  
**Owner scenes:** `godot/player/player.tscn`, `godot/player/bullet/bullet.tscn`, `godot/enemy/enemy.tscn`  
**Scripts:** `player.gd:153-165`, `bullet.gd`, `enemy.gd:34-47`  
**`[MISSING]`** No player health. No kill count. No score for eliminations. Enemies pose no threat to the player.

### S-03 — Collection System
**Domain:** Coin pickup and count display  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Spatial reward for navigation; provides visible progress feedback.  
**Owner scenes:** `godot/coin/coin.tscn`, `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Scripts:** `coin.gd`, `player.gd:47-51`  
**State:** `Player.coins` (int, session-only — no persistence)  
**`[MISSING]`** Coin total display, collection-complete event, save/load.

### S-04 — Camera System
**Domain:** Third-person follow camera with obstruction avoidance  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Maintain visibility in complex 3D geometry without requiring manual camera input from the player.  
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `follow_camera.gd`  
**Core variables:** difference (orbit vector), three PhysicsServer3D raycasts, collision_exception (Array[RID])

### S-05 — Rendering System
**Domain:** Visual quality and renderer compatibility  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Support both modern GPU (Forward+) and legacy/mobile (gl_compatibility) without separate projects.  
**Owner scene:** `godot/stage/stage.tscn`

**gl_compatibility path:** PCF13 (`SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_HIGH`), energy split across sky-only and light-only duplicate `[OBSERVED stage.gd:4-14]`

### S-06 — Audio System

**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Reinforce mechanical events — jump, shoot, coin, enemy death.  
**Assets:** `SoundJump` (player), `SoundShoot` (player), `SoundWalkLoop` (enemy loop), `SoundHit` (enemy)  
**Bus layout:** `godot/default_bus_layout.tres`  
**`[MISSING]`** Background music. Coin collect audio not confirmed in player.gd (may be in coin animation).

### S-07 — Input System
**Domain:** Control mapping across keyboard, gamepad, touch  
**Design reason:** `[INFERRED]` Single input action layer enables multi-platform control without branching game code.  
**Registered actions** `[OBSERVED project.godot:96-145]`: `move_forward`, `move_back`, `move_left`, `move_right`, `jump`, `shoot`, `reset_position`, `ui_accept`, `ui_cancel`, `ui_left`, `ui_right`, `ui_up`, `ui_down`

## 08. PROGRESSION

**`[MISSING]`** No progression system is implemented. No multiple levels, no checkpoint, no difficulty ramp, no unlock gate, no level transition.

**`[INFERRED]`** Implicit spatial progression: coin clusters distributed across the level at increasing distance from spawn; enemy placement creates soft gates near some coin groups; higher-elevation platforms require multi-jump navigation. The level has one discovered secret area (lower room reachable by normal inputs) `[OBSERVED FRICTIONAL.md]`.

**Skill curve `[MISSING design]`:** Level is open; all areas nominally accessible from spawn. Difficulty is topographic (jump precision and fall recovery) rather than designed gate sequences.

**Resource curve `[OBSERVED]`:** 73 coins, no respawn, session-only count, no maximum displayed.

## 16. UI/UX

### Diegetic (in 3D world space)

## Zelda's Notes

*Silent mode — pushback written here, not spoken.*

**Ghost Center (Failure Mode 1 — present).**  
The session has no goal. There is no win state, no fail state, no reason to collect all 73 coins rather than 2. The player can play indefinitely, collect nothing, or quit immediately. This is acceptable for a teaching demo if labeled explicitly. It is a production problem if the film claims this is a "game." Before narration is written, someone must answer OQ-01: what does success look like for the player?

**Mechanic Mirage (Failure Mode 2 — partial).**  
Enemies cannot harm the player. They patrol, they topple when shot, but the only consequence of ignoring them is a moving obstacle in the path of coin collection. This removes meaningful tension from the shoot mechanic. A player who never shoots still collects all 73 coins. If the teaching goal is "demonstrate RigidBody3D contact detection," the mechanic is complete. If the goal is "create challenge," it is not.

**Scope Concentration.**  
11 of 16 listed features are CORE by any reasonable definition — but this is a recovered build, not a scoped list. The core percentage reflects implementation completeness, not design prioritization. Before planning, answer: which of these features the Walker film must demonstrate, and which are present by inheritance from the upstream demo?

**What the code's structure suggests the vision was `[INFERRED]`:**  
A Godot 4.7 CharacterBody3D movement showcase. The quality of the movement system — camera-relative input, physics-interpolated 120 Hz, variable jump, smooth mesh arc rotation, air factor tuning — is the work of someone who cared about character feel. That level of care is absent from the session structure (no win state, no narrative). The Walker brief confirms it: "establish what it actually implements and verify that behavior." This is a proof of mechanics, not a shipped game.

**Next command:**  
Run `/gdd v1` to fill the missing intent — target player, design pillars, win state, and player fantasy. Or run `/gdd draft` to generate rough drafts of all sections with assumptions flagged for iteration.

## 03. DESIGN PILLARS

`[MISSING]` No explicit design pillars are documented in any source file.

Zelda's read — pillars inferred from code structure and the Walker brief. These require human confirmation before any design decision references them.

**Pillar A — Grounded Physical Movement**  
*Player experience it protects:* The character must feel like it has mass and respond to momentum.  
*Evidence:* Jolt Physics at 120 Hz; gravity=22.0 m/s² (2.24× Earth); AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL=false (no air stopping); AIR_ACCEL_FACTOR=0.5 (limited air authority); sharp-turn threshold at 140° breaks momentum. The character decelerates into a direction change rather than snapping. `[INFERRED from player.gd constants]`  
*What violates it:* instant-stop air movement, floaty gravity, unrestricted air steering.

**Pillar B — Readable Camera**  
*Player experience it protects:* The player sees what matters without fighting the camera.  
*Evidence:* Three-ray autoturn system pushes camera away from geometry before it clips. Obstruction pull moves camera to collision point as worst case. Top-level detach prevents parenting artifacts. Height clamped [0, 2] prevents floor-skating view. `[INFERRED from follow_camera.gd]`  
*What violates it:* camera clipping into geometry, manual camera rotation added without autoturn integration.

**Pillar C — Inspectability**  
*Player experience it protects (for the Walker/learning audience):* Every mechanism is readable from source.  
*Evidence:* 8 scripts, no AutoLoads, no scene-specific game manager, all feature logic self-contained in owning scene scripts. `[INFERRED from GAME-BRIEF.md and codebase structure]`  
*What violates it:* global state, singletons that hide flow, cross-scene coupling.

### M-01 — Ground Movement
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd`  
**Node:** CharacterBody3D (class Player)  
**Input actions:** `move_forward` (W/↑/LStick-Y-), `move_back` (S/↓/LStick-Y+), `move_left` (A/←/LStick-X-), `move_right` (D/→/LStick-X+)

Camera-relative horizontal movement. `Input.get_vector()` produces a 2D input; it is rotated into the camera's basis then projected onto the XZ plane (Y zeroed, renormalized). Separate `horizontal_direction` and `horizontal_speed` allow smooth arc turning via `adjust_facing()`.

Sharp turn detection: if moving speed >0.1 and angle between movement direction and current heading >140°, acceleration is suppressed. The player must decelerate before reversing direction. `[OBSERVED player.gd:73-74]`

Mesh rotation uses `adjust_facing()` — angular interpolation toward movement direction, rate weighted by `TURN_SPEED / speed`. `[OBSERVED player.gd:97-115, 179-202]`

### M-03 — Variable Jump
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/player.gd:117-137`  
**Input action:** `jump` (Space / Mouse RMB / Gamepad A)

Jump initiates only when `is_on_floor()` is true and `jumping` flag is false. Sets `vertical_velocity = JUMP_VELOCITY`, sets `jumping = true`, plays SoundJump. ### M-06 — Shooting
**Owner scenes:** `godot/player/player.tscn`, `godot/player/bullet/bullet.tscn`

### M-08 — Enemy Patrol
**Owner scene:** `godot/enemy/enemy.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/enemy/enemy.gd`  
**Node:** RigidBody3D

Floor ray (`_ray_floor: RayCast3D`) and wall ray (`_ray_wall: RayCast3D`) evaluated in `_integrate_forces`. `advance = _ray_floor.is_colliding() and not _ray_wall.is_colliding()`. On advance: accelerate along current facing direction; decelerate on perpendicular (lateral) axis. On not-advance: rotate in place using `Basis(up, rot_dir * ROT_SPEED * delta)`. `rot_dir` initializes to 4.0; resets to 1.0 when the enemy transitions from advance to turn (`prev_advance → false`). `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:49-73]`

4 enemy instances at fixed world positions. `[OBSERVED game.tscn]`

### M-09 — Enemy Death
**Owner scene:** `godot/enemy/enemy.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/enemy/enemy.gd:34-47, 77-78`

Detected in `_integrate_forces` via contact loop. On contact with a Bullet where `bullet.enabled == true`: set `dying = true`, unlock all rotation axes (`axis_lock_angular_*= false`), set `collision_layer = 0` (removes from collision), apply angular spin (`-contact_normal.cross(up).normalized() * 33.0`), queue animation "impact" then "extra/explode", set `bullet.enabled = false`, stop SoundWalkLoop, play SoundHit. Returns immediately; remaining contacts ignored. `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:34-47]`

`_die()` called by animation signal (end of explode): `queue_free()`. `[OBSERVED enemy.gd:77-78]`

### M-10 — Follow Camera
**Owner scene:** `godot/player/player.tscn`  
**Script:** `godot/player/follow_camera.gd`  
**Node:** Camera3D

In `_ready()`: finds ancestor RigidBody3D or CharacterBody3D and stores its RID in `collision_exception` (prevents camera rays from hitting player/enemies). Calls `set_as_top_level(true)` to decouple transform from parent. `[OBSERVED follow_camera.gd:16-29]`

In `_physics_process()`: computes `difference = cam_pos - target`. Clamps length to [min_distance, max_distance]. Clamps Y component to [MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_HEIGHT]. Casts three rays from target to `target + difference` at 0°, +autoturn_aperture°, -autoturn_aperture°. Result: center blocked → move camera to hit point; only left blocked → rotate right; only right blocked → rotate left; both sides blocked, center clear → no autoturn. Applies `look_at_from_position` then optional vertical tilt. `[OBSERVED follow_camera.gd:32-91]`

Enemies cannot harm the player. They patrol, they topple when shot, but the only consequence of ignoring them is a moving obstacle in the path of coin collection. 02 — Vision

OBSERVED GAME-BRIEF.md
A blue robot moves through a textured 3D platform environment, jumps between surfaces, collects coins, and shoots projectiles at patrolling enemies. A camera follows the character and responds to obstructing geometry.
WALKER CONTEXT OBSERVED
  • Adaptation of Godot official 3D Platformer demo
  • Initial change: project name only
  • Controls, art, sound preserved from upstream
  • Teaching loop: Brief → Build → Playtest → Inspect → Revise
CRITICAL GAPS MISSING
  • Logline — none documented
  • Target player — not defined
  • Win state — no session goal
  • Design pillars — not written
INFERRED Teaching intent: demonstrates CharacterBody3D movement, camera following, collectibles, enemy patrol — inspectable by Godot students.

03 — Design Pillars INFERRED — requires human confirmation

A — Grounded Physical Movement
What it protects: character must feel mass and momentum cost
  • Jolt Physics 120 Hz
  • Gravity = 22.0 m/s² (2.24× Earth)
  • AIR_IDLE_DEACCEL = false
  • Air accel factor = 0.5
  • Sharp turn >140° breaks momentum
B — Readable Camera
What it protects: player sees action without fighting camera
  • Three-ray autoturn ±25°
  • Obstruction pull to collision point
  • Top-level detach (no parent artifact)
  • Height clamped [0, 2]
  • Autoturn speed: 50°/s
C — Inspectability
What it protects: every mechanism readable from source
  • 8 scripts, no AutoLoads
  • No cross-scene coupling
  • Feature logic in owning scene
  • Walker brief: inspect & verify
  • No singleton state managers
All three pillars inferred from code structure and GAME-BRIEF.md. Run /gdd v2 to define them explicitly with human input.

MACRO 30–120 s

SESSION — [MISSING]
